newsitem.title: USA: Warmth aids Nebraska crops, development lags avg.
newsitem.headline: Warmth aids Nebraska crops, development lags avg.

text.p: Above normal temperatures boosted Nebraska corn and soybean progress, but row crop development remained one to two weeks behind average, according to the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.

Corn was rated three percent poor, 14 percent fair, 56 percent good and 27 percent excellent. The crop was 96 percent in the dough stage or beyond, in line with the five-year average. One percent of the acreage had reached full maturity, lagging average of 16 percent.
There were reports of gray leaf spot problems in the southern and eastern portions of the state.
Soybeans were rated two percent poor, 17 percent fair, 50 percent good and 31 percent excellent. Fourteen percent of the acreage had turned color, well behind average of 40 percent.
Winter wheat was 11 percent planted, slightly behind last year's pace of 13 percent.
Topsoil moisture was rated one percent very short, 27 percent short, 67 percent adequate and five percent surplus.
Pasture and range were rated one percent very poor, seven percent poor, 24 percent fair, 52 percent good and 16 percent excellent.
